```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(car) # For VIF analysis

# Load the datasets
zip_income_data <- read_csv("/Users/yining/Downloads/21zpallagi.csv")
medicare_data <- read_csv("/Users/yining/Downloads/Medicare_Physician_Other_Practitioners_by_Geography_and_Service_2022.csv")

# Step 1: Create a mapping of state abbreviations to full names
state_mapping <- data.frame(
  state_abbrev = c("AL", "AK", "AZ", "AR", "CA", "CO", "CT", "DE", "FL", "GA", "HI", "ID", "IL", "IN", 
                   "IA", "KS", "KY", "LA", "ME", "MD", "MA", "MI", "MN", "MS", "MO", "MT", "NE", "NV", 
                   "NH", "NJ", "NM", "NY", "NC", "ND", "OH", "OK", "OR", "PA", "RI", "SC", "SD", "TN", 
                   "TX", "UT", "VT", "VA", "WA", "WV", "WI", "WY"),
  state_full = c("Alabama", "Alaska", "Arizona", "Arkansas", "California", "Colorado", "Connecticut", 
                 "Delaware", "Florida", "Georgia", "Hawaii", "Idaho", "Illinois", "Indiana", "Iowa", 
                 "Kansas", "Kentucky", "Louisiana", "Maine", "Maryland", "Massachusetts", "Michigan", 
                 "Minnesota", "Mississippi", "Missouri", "Montana", "Nebraska", "Nevada", "New Hampshire", 
                 "New Jersey", "New Mexico", "New York", "North Carolina", "North Dakota", "Ohio", 
                 "Oklahoma", "Oregon", "Pennsylvania", "Rhode Island", "South Carolina", "South Dakota", 
                 "Tennessee", "Texas", "Utah", "Vermont", "Virginia", "Washington", "West Virginia", 
                 "Wisconsin", "Wyoming")
)

# Step 2: Preprocess ZIP income data
zip_income_data_clean <- zip_income_data %>%
  filter(agi_stub >= 1 & agi_stub <= 6) %>% # Include valid AGI ranges
  select(zipcode, A00100, A00200, N1, state = STATE) %>%  # Select relevant columns and state abbreviation
  rename(
    avg_income = A00100, # Average income
    wage_amount = A00200, # Wages
    num_returns = N1      # Number of returns
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_income = as.numeric(avg_income),
    wage_amount = as.numeric(wage_amount),
    num_returns = as.numeric(num_returns)
  ) %>%
  left_join(state_mapping, by = c("state" = "state_abbrev")) # Add full state names

# Step 3: Aggregate ZIP income data to state level using full state names
state_income_data <- zip_income_data_clean %>%
  group_by(state_full) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_income = mean(avg_income, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_wages = sum(wage_amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_returns = sum(num_returns, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Step 4: Preprocess Medicare data
medicare_data_clean <- medicare_data %>%
  mutate(
    Avg_Mdcr_Pymt_Amt = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", Avg_Mdcr_Pymt_Amt)), # Clean and convert to numeric
    Tot_Srvcs = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", Tot_Srvcs))                  # Clean and convert to numeric
  ) %>%
  filter(
    grepl("sugar", HCPCS_Desc, ignore.case = TRUE), # Focus on glucose-related services (they achieve the same purpose)
    !is.na(Avg_Mdcr_Pymt_Amt) & !is.na(Tot_Srvcs),  # Remove rows with NA values
    Tot_Srvcs > 0                                   # Exclude rows with zero services
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_reimbursement = Avg_Mdcr_Pymt_Amt * Tot_Srvcs # Calculate total reimbursement
  ) %>%
  rename(state_full = Rndrng_Prvdr_Geo_Desc) %>%
  group_by(state_full) %>%
  summarise(
    total_reimbursement = sum(total_reimbursement, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_services = sum(Tot_Srvcs, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Step 5: Merge datasets on state_full
merged_data <- state_income_data %>%
  inner_join(medicare_data_clean, by = "state_full")

# Inspect merged data
head(merged_data)

# Step 6: Visualize the relationship between average income and Medicare reimbursements
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_income, y = total_reimbursement)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Average Income and Glucose Related Reimbursements",
    x = "Average Income (in thousands)",
    y = "Total Medicare Reimbursement (in dollars)"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Step 9: Analyze Geographic Disparities
plot_usmap(data = state_map_data, values = "total_reimbursement", regions = "states") +
  scale_fill_continuous(low = "white", high = "blue", name = "Total Reimbursements") +
  labs(
    title = "Medicare Reimbursements for Blood Glucose Related Expenditures by State",
    subtitle = "Analyzing regional disparities in reimbursements"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

# Step 10: Correlation matrix to explore relationships
ggcorrplot(cor_matrix, method = "circle", type = "lower", 
           title = "Correlation Matrix of Key Variables") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Step 11: Feature Importance Analysis Using Random Forest
ggplot(var_importance, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Feature Importance from Random Forest",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Step 12: Residuals vs Fitted values
ggplot(data = data.frame(residuals = residuals(model), fitted = fitted(model)), aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted Values",
    y = "Residuals"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Check normality of residuals
ggplot(data = data.frame(residuals = residuals(model)), aes(x = residuals)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Residuals",
    x = "Residuals",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Step 13: Predictive Analysis
ggplot(new_data, aes(x = avg_income, y = predicted_reimbursement)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Reimbursements vs Average Income",
    x = "Average Income (in thousands)",
    y = "Predicted Medicare Reimbursement"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```
